newsitem.title: HUNGARY: HUNGARY NOON RADIO HEADLINES - MARCH 6.
newsitem.headline: HUNGARY NOON RADIO HEADLINES - MARCH 6.

text.p: These are the main headlines on Hungary's Kossuth Radio midday news. Reuters cannot vouch for their accuracy:
- Farmers' demonstrations against 1997 tax rules continue, while the government discusses planned amendments on the law which regulates the tax-payments of agricultural producers.
- The trade union of public education employees expressed dissatifaction over delays in the transfer of surplus wages promised by the government to public employees, the trade union said.
- Senior Budapest municipality officials said mass transport services would not be curbed in the capital this year.
- Austria keeps up the strict customs control of trucks on its border with Hungary.
- The Foreign Ministry recommended Hungarians planning to visit Albania to get informed about the situation in the southern European country.
- Postabank has not decided yet whether it will compensate depositors who pulled out their money of the bank before maturity in a five-day panic run which ended on Monday.
- The police detained a person for alleged illegal production of arms in the southeast Hungarian town Mako.
